title: PowerShell steganography loader opens LSASS with full-access masks on scranton
rationale: All describe the same event: PowerShell.exe PID 2976 on scranton.dmevals.local opened lsass.exe PID 736 at 2020-05-02T03:05:16Z with GrantedAccess 0x1F3FFF and 0x1FFFFF, call trace ending in UNKNOWN modules. This is LSASS memory access consistent with credential dumping (T1003.001). F36/F47/F53 add context (no auth-process modification, no Kerberos theft, preceded by cert export) but center on the same LSASS handle events.

title: wsmprovhost.exe PowerShell remoting session opens LSASS with 0x1F3FFF on nashua
rationale: Both describe the same event: wsmprovhost.exe PID 7720 on nashua.dmevals.local opened lsass.exe PID 728 at 2020-05-02T03:09:29Z with GrantedAccess 0x1F3FFF via a PowerShell cmdlet call trace. LSASS access from a remoting host is best mapped to T1003.001, though confidence is medium given the Get-Process cmdlet context.

title: Get-Keystrokes keylogger job on scranton
rationale: Get-Keystrokes job invoked, viewed and removed in pbeesly's PowerShell is keyboard input capture, matching T1056.001.

title: PowerShell screen-capture (GUI input capture) on scranton
rationale: Invoke-ScreenCapture function looping CopyFromScreen to save .bmp files is GUI input capture, matching T1056.002.

title: Cleartext credentials in files and command lines on scranton (Invoke-Exfil, PsExec64)
rationale: These describe credentials embedded in files and command lines: Invoke-Exfil's plaintext cozy/MyCozyPassw0rd!, the OfficeSupplies.7z archive, and PsExec64.exe launched with -u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by against \\NASHUA. Credentials in files/command lines map to T1552.001.

title: PowerShell on nashua collects credential-keyword files into working.zip
rationale: Recursive ChildItem for *pass*, *login*, *admin*, *vpn and similar files compressed into working.zip is collection of credentials in files, matching T1552.001.

title: PowerShell credential harvesting and exfil staging (clipboard, archive, cleanup) on scranton
rationale: Get-Clipboard harvesting followed by Invoke-Exfil staging and Invoke-BeachCleanup deleting collected artifacts; clipboard credential harvesting is best mapped to T1555.003 (credentials from password stores/web browsers context) as the closest in-scope technique.

title: Get-PrivateKeys certificate export to password-protected .pfx on scranton
rationale: All describe the same action: the attacker-staged readme.ps1 toolkit (renamed from readme.txt and dot-sourced) defined and ran Get-PrivateKeys, exporting every LocalMachine certificate with private keys to .pfx files protected by hardcoded password 'saribas'. Stealing authentication certificates/private keys best fits T1649.

title: csc.exe runtime compilation of attacker DLLs from PowerShell on scranton
rationale: Add-Type/csc.exe compiling DLLs in Temp is runtime code compilation for execution, not credential access; best mapped to T1027.004.

title: Screensaver payload drops steganographic monkey.png on scranton
rationale: Explorer launching C:\ProgramData\victim\cod.3aka3.scr which wrote monkey.png is initial payload delivery/execution, not credential access; best mapped to T1204 (User Execution).

title: hostui.exe -verb runas elevation and registry-value Invoke-Expression on scranton
rationale: Start-Process hostui.exe -verb runas followed by registry-value IEX and reflective loader is privilege escalation/execution, best mapped to T1548.002 (Bypass User Account Control).

title: sdclt.exe UAC-bypass pattern with HKCU Folder shell open command on scranton
rationale: sdclt.exe launches with HKCU\Software\Classes\Folder\shell\open\command DelegateExecute manipulation is a UAC bypass, best mapped to T1548.002.
